nodes.description: A patent publication titled "Real-time ad-hoc spam filtering of email" describing a multi-pass ad-hoc spam message filtering approach.

A filtering approach that dynamically generates a temporary classifier during a first pass based on results of a previously applied message filter that sorts messages into folders, then uses the classifier in a second pass to retrospectively inspect messages for misclassification.
A model generated during the first pass analysis of messages, configured to reside exclusively in a non-persistent memory location and purged after use.

A message filter configured to sort messages into different message folders and to store first classification data in a persistent store.<SEP>A message filter that previously sorts messages into a plurality of different message folders and stores first classification data in a persistent store.<SEP>A message filter that sorts messages into different message folders and stores first classification data in a persistent store; it is automatically executed independent of user action.
A filter configured to generate a classification model based on a first pass analysis and use it to perform a second pass on sorted messages to identify misclassified messages.

A device distinct from a client device on which the first message filter is configured to execute.<SEP>A device comprising a transceiver to send and receive data over a network and a processor operative to perform multi-pass message filtering actions.<SEP>A device configured to receive messages, assign them to message folders using the first message filter, and communicate the messages over a network to the message folders.
A component of the network device that sends and receives data over a network.
A component of the network device operative to perform actions including first and second pass analyses of messages.

A plurality of different folders into which messages are sorted by the first message filter.<SEP>Different folders into which messages are sorted; a message may be identified as sorted into an incorrect message folder and a user may move it to another folder.
A generated identification of sorted messages that might be misclassified, displayed so a user can move misclassified messages to different folders.
A memory-resident-only location where the generated classification model resides, not stored on disk or another persistent data store.

A storage location where the first message filter is configured to store first classification data.<SEP>A persistent data store where the first message filter stores first classification data.<SEP>A storage location where the first message filter stores first classification data.

A device on which the first pass and second pass of the multi-pass message filter may execute entirely, and on which the first pass is executed to train the multi-pass message filter.<SEP>A user's device on which the classification model is maintained in memory and where the first and second passes may occur entirely.<SEP>A device on which the multi-pass message filter is executed, where second classification data resides exclusively in non-persistent memory, and which provides a display of information about misclassified messages.

A storage medium readable by a processor that stores instructions for executing the multi-pass message filter and related operations.<SEP>A medium including data and instructions whose execution on a computing device provides for managing messages.
An email message that is received, sorted, analyzed, and scored by the message filters.
Information within messages read during the first pass, including sender address and whether the sender's address is in an address book.
Header information within messages, including a subject and an originating network address, read during the first pass.
The content of messages read during the first pass analysis.
Attachments within messages read during the first pass analysis.

An address book associated with a recipient that is associated with the message folders, used in generating the classification model.<SEP>An address book associated with a recipient that is associated with the message folders; a message sender's address in the address book may be analyzed to generate second classification data.
A value assigned to each message during the second pass used to identify messages sorted into an incorrect message folder.

A message filtering method that executes in multiple passes, including a first pass on a client device to train the filter by generating second classification data, and a second pass that deletes the second classification data so it is no longer accessible.<SEP>A message filter executed in multiple passes on a client device; a first pass trains the filter by generating second classification data, and a second pass uses that data to score each message.
A classifier that the multi-pass message filter may employ.
Classification data stored in a persistent store by the first message filter.<SEP>Classification data generated by the first message filter and stored in a persistent store.

Classification data generated during the first pass of the multi-pass message filter to train the filter, which is deleted in the second pass so it is no longer accessible.<SEP>Classification data generated by the first pass of the multi-pass message filter to train the filter; it resides exclusively in a non-persistent memory store and is deleted upon providing the display of information.
A classification model generated based on an analysis of at least which message folder a message currently resides.
One of a plurality of different folders into which messages are sorted, and whose contents are analyzed to generate the second classification model.

A method for managing message delivery that includes receiving messages, sorting them into folders using a first message filter, and executing a first pass of a multi-pass message filter on a client device.
A memory store on the client device where the second classification data resides exclusively and from which it is deleted upon providing the display of information.
Communications received and sorted into message folders, each scored by the multi-pass message filter.
The network over which the network device communicates messages to the message folders.
A person enabled to move an identified message to another message folder and able to select execution of the multi-pass message filter through an interface on the client device.
An interface on the client device through which a user can select execution of the multi-pass message filter.
A header of a message that may be analyzed to generate second classification data.
The content of a message that may be analyzed to generate second classification data.
A score assigned to each message by the second pass of the multi-pass message filter, used to identify messages sorted into an incorrect message folder.

The multi-pass filtering approach generates its classifier based on results of the previously applied first message filter.
The second multi-pass message filter generates a classification model based on first pass analysis and uses it in a second pass.
The generated classification model is configured to reside exclusively in a non-persistent memory location.
The classification model is maintained within memory on a user's client device.
The processor purges the generated classification model from the non-persistent memory location.
The classification model is generated based on analysis of sender information such as the sender's address in an address book.
The classification model is generated based on analysis of a header of a message.
The classification model is generated based on analysis of message content.
The first pass reads attachments among the information used to create the classification model.
The first message filter sorts messages into a plurality of different message folders.
The first message filter is configured to store first classification data in a persistent store.<SEP>The first message filter stores first classification data in a persistent store.
The storage medium includes instructions for sorting messages using the first message filter.
The first message filter is configured to execute on a network device distinct from a client device.<SEP>The network device assigns messages to message folders using the first message filter.
The first message filter is configured to store first classification data in a persistent store.
The first message filter sorts a plurality of messages into a plurality of different message folders.
The method for managing message delivery sorts messages into folders using a first message filter.
The first message filter sorts the plurality of messages into different message folders.
The second multi-pass message filter generates a misclassification identification of sorted messages.
The second multi-pass message filter performs passes on the sorted messages in the message folders.
The processor is operative to perform first and second pass analyses using the second multi-pass message filter.
The second pass of the multi-pass message filter scores each message.
The storage medium includes instructions for executing first and second passes of the multi-pass message filter.
Executing the first pass and second pass of the multi-pass message filter occurs entirely on a client device.
The network device comprises a transceiver to send and receive data over a network.
The network device comprises a processor operative to perform message filtering actions.
The network device receives the plurality of messages and assigns them to message folders using the first message filter.
The network device communicates the messages over the network to the message folders.
The network device communicates the messages over the network to the plurality of different message folders.
The misclassification identification is displayed such that a misclassified message can be moved to a different message folder.
A message's score indicates whether the message is sorted into an incorrect message folder.
The plurality of messages is sorted and assigned into a plurality of different message folders.
A message's respective score indicates whether the message is sorted into an incorrect message folder.
A user is enabled to move an identified message to another message folder.
The second classification data is generated based on which folder each of the plurality of messages resides.

The first pass and second pass of the multi-pass message filter may occur entirely on a client device, and the first pass is executed on a client device to train the multi-pass message filter.<SEP>The multi-pass message filter is executed on the client device in a first pass and a second pass.
The second classification data is deleted from the client device upon providing the display of information.

Execution of instructions on the processor readable storage medium provides for managing messages.

The second classification data is generated based on an analysis of whether a message sender's address is in an address book associated with a recipient.

The first pass of the multi-pass message filter generates second classification data to train the filter, and the second pass deletes the second classification data so it is no longer accessible.<SEP>The first pass of the multi-pass message filter trains the filter by generating second classification data.
The multi-pass message filter employs a Naive Bayes classifier.
The second pass of the multi-pass message filter uses the second classification data to score each message.
The method for managing message delivery executes, on a client device, a first pass of a multi-pass message filter on the sorted messages.
The multi-pass message filter is selectable for execution by a user through an interface on the client device.
The second classification data is configured to reside exclusively in a non-persistent memory store.
The second classification data is generated based on an analysis of a header of a message.
